summary.intent: Build, for the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge, an agent-based product that continuously monitors Soony's launch data drops, finds contradictions the ERP/plan hides, and acts (supplier emails, escalations, approvals); then polish it, prepare a demo and hand it in by Sunday 12:00.
summary.outcome: Analysed the confidential data and found the real launch risks (overbooked art book receipt, failed statue lot, stuck containers, rev B/C sleeve conflict). Built and deployed a Python/React app with a polling loop, versioned store, extraction agent, routines, a sign-off loop and a separate dry-run demo instance. Committed and pushed most work, and fixed many UI and wiring bugs; a few commits are still unpushed.

repo: Confidential portal data lives only in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token and .env.example is committed. Never put data values in code or the repo.
The portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Change detection must poll and compare SHA-256, because files are replaced under the same name.
Teammates use CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md as a team workflow; claim tasks in PROGRESS.md before building. Work happens on branch jonas/today-flow.

The live instance sends real supplier emails. A separate demo instance (scripts/demo.sh reset|snapshot|stop, host ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev, dry mail outbox, polling/sync off) exists for rehearsals.
Entire only creates a checkpoint when repo files change; checkpoints are pushed with git push.
Push notifications go to every subscribed device; there is no per-person targeting, so 'Sent to Maren's phone' is only true if her phone is the subscriber.
ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK is empty in .env, so nothing reaches Teams; ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds> auto-approves passed-on cases in a demo, marked as simulated.

code.finding: Implements the sign-off loop: one-time /ok/<token> links, Approve/Decline, simulated approval timer, and recording via=signoff. basic_auth.py lets valid links bypass the password.

J/K navigation must step per list row (folded group counts as one) and keep a group's row highlighted while any case in it is open. Also holds the 'Ready for your OK' group, which is shown per routine.

workflow: A fixed, non-AI polling loop outside with agents inside, and plain code for the numbers, keeps results checkable and cheap.
Parallel builder subagents work well for sizeable features while the main thread writes docs; they leave changes uncommitted and the server needs a restart after backend changes.
Verify UI changes with headless browser screenshots and scripted checks (for example pressing J ten times and counting highlighted rows).
Prepared proposals must expire when their case is decided, otherwise the UI offers actions the server rightly refuses.
A shared mailbox sync wrote back a stale action log and lost a record (lost-update race); appending under a shared lock fixed it.
Hackathon scoring rewards a few real stories over fixing everything: judges score the pitch, business case, depth, taste and a live demo, not whether the launch is saved.

friction: Portal token was empty at first, blocking all data work until the user supplied it.
Entire looked inactive because no checkpoint was written when no repo files had changed.
Routine option matching searched for the literal text 'make po,rev', so the routine ran but sent nothing.
Four prepared 'Do all 4' steps failed with 'not an open card' because their cases had already been decided by hand.
Internal messages and escalations were only recorded, yet the UI claimed 'DC site lead has it now', which was false.
Cloudflare Error 1033 on the demo host came from DNS first being attached to the wrong tunnel.
Safari caches favicons stubbornly, so the old yellow icon may persist.
Duplicate identical routines produced duplicate prepared steps.
The PackRight rev C request was sent twice more after the supplier had already replied.
The top bar says 'nothing needs you' for Maren because it counts Felix's list.
open_items: Push the unpushed commits (dry mail, demo script, favicon, J/K, and later wording fixes).
Delete the duplicate 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock' routine on live (awaiting the user's decision).
Set up a Teams webhook (ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK) so internal messages and escalations reach a real channel.
Build the 'What still saves it' section on Launch (latest arrival per blocker, about 900 copies per hour of delay).
Add the Felix office-hours question about who moves container NHSU4471921 to the DC today.
Write the 3-minute demo script and pitch outline, record the video, and finish the README before the 12:00 hand-in.
Make the Launch header say the next decision-by time; fix the top bar for Maren's role.
Add per-person push targeting; undo does not recall an already sent push.
Reply to Boise on EXW versus DDP terms and send PackRight the rev C file and change notice.
The earlier Claude docs and the older briefing artifact still show the 14:00 state; the portal login password was shared in Discord and should be changed after the hack.
Commit the in-progress wording fixes (status sentence, who decides/signs) and the stop-label change.
